I read the transcript and the repo's steering files. Here's what went wrong and what I'd change, worst first.

## 1. Root cause of the bug: agent hand-edited a generated file instead of the schema source of truth
The agent added `currency` directly to `src/db/generated-types.ts:10-15`, which is headed `// AUTO-GENERATED. Do not edit.` and whose own generator (`scripts/gen-types.ts`) rewrites it from `src/db/schema.ts`. But `src/db/schema.ts:11-17` (`refunds`) was never touched — it still has no `currency` field. The moment anyone runs `pnpm db:generate` (which `gen-types.ts` says must happen "after any change to schema.ts"), the hand-added field gets silently overwritten — exactly the "currency field disappeared" report, and plausibly why CI went red (downstream code referencing `Refund.currency` stops typechecking once the file regenerates).

CLAUDE.md already has the right rule ("Never commit generated files by hand") but it's a passive bullet buried in a list, not something the agent connected to this specific edit.
- **`CLAUDE.md`**: add a concrete instruction under "Rules" or "Where things are": *"DB shape changes start in `src/db/schema.ts`, then run `pnpm db:generate`. Never hand-edit `src/db/generated-types.ts`."*
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**: add a step that runs `pnpm db:generate` and fails on a diff (`git diff --exit-code`), so drift between schema and generated types is caught in CI, not the next morning.

## 2. Internal-import boundary rule exists but nothing enforces it
The agent imported `query` from `../internal/pg-driver.js` into `src/core/router.ts:2`, despite CLAUDE.md's explicit rule ("Never import from `src/internal/*` outside the module that owns it") and the file's own header comment ("Internal. Owned by `src/db`. Do not import from elsewhere."). This also contradicts `docs/architecture/request-flow.md:8` ("Handlers never touch the database driver directly"). Nothing caught it — `eslint.config.js` has no import-boundary rule, and the reviewer agent only checked `CODING_STANDARDS.md`.
- **`eslint.config.js`**: add `no-restricted-imports` (or `eslint-plugin-boundaries`) rules that block imports of `src/internal/**` from outside `src/db/**`.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**: it never runs `pnpm lint` at all — add that step.

## 3. `any` usage crept in, and nothing in tooling or review blocks it
`orderRepo.ts` grew a `findRefund` returning `any`, violating CLAUDE.md's "Never use `any`" rule — the agent noted this was a shortcut and moved on. `eslint.config.js` uses plain `js.configs.recommended`, no `@typescript-eslint` rules, so `any` is invisible to lint. The reviewer agent also didn't catch it because it only checked `CODING_STANDARDS.md` (error-message voice), not `CLAUDE.md`'s rules.
- **`eslint.config.js`**: pull in `typescript-eslint` and enable `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`.
- **`CODING_STANDARDS.md`**: it currently says "Read during review, not during implementation" as if it's the only review checklist. Add a line that review also verifies compliance with `CLAUDE.md`'s rules, not just style.

## 4. CLAUDE.md tells the agent to run a script that doesn't exist
`CLAUDE.md:36` says "Run `pnpm test:unit` before every commit," but `package.json` has no `test:unit` script — only `test`. The agent hit `ERR_PNPM_NO_SCRIPT` and had to guess. Small but it's a steering file giving a wrong instruction, which erodes trust in the rest of it.
- **`CLAUDE.md`**: change `pnpm test:unit` → `pnpm test`.

## 5. `pnpm dev` silences all output, so runtime verification is impossible
`package.json:5`: `"dev": "tsx watch src/cli/serve.ts > /dev/null 2>&1"`. The agent started it to confirm the endpoint worked, saw nothing, retried twice, and gave up — not because of agent error, the script actively discards stdout/stderr. This blocks both agents and humans from ever seeing server logs.
- **`package.json`**: drop the `> /dev/null 2>&1` redirect from the `dev` script.

## 6. Mandatory `pnpm status-report` step is pure noise for most tasks
CLAUDE.md:7-8 requires running it before *any* task. It `cat`s `docs/status-dump.txt`, a 419-line synthetic dump of unrelated module states — confirmed nothing in it was relevant to a refunds/currency task. This burns context on every single session for no benefit.
- **`CLAUDE.md`**: either drop this requirement, or scope it ("only relevant when touching deploy/module-health code") rather than blanket-requiring it.

## 7. Two steering files directly contradict each other on export style
`CLAUDE.md:16`: "Prefer named exports over default exports." `CODING_STANDARDS.md:9`: "Prefer default exports for single-export modules." Didn't bite this session, but it will produce a coin-flip result (and a confused review comment) the first time it's relevant.
- **`CLAUDE.md`** or **`CODING_STANDARDS.md`**: reconcile to one rule — most likely drop the `CODING_STANDARDS.md` line, since CLAUDE.md's "named exports" rule is unconditional and this one only applies to a special case.
